ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the Cartesian coordinate system, point O is the origin. The parabola $y = ax^2 + bx + 3$ passes through points $B(-3, 0)$ and $C(1, 0)$, and intersects the y-axis at point A. As shown in Figure 1, point P lies on the parabola. A line through point P parallel to the y-axis intersects the line segment $AB$ at point D. Denoting the x-coordinate of point P as t, and the length of segment $PD$ as d, find the functional expression of d in terms of t (it is not required to state the domain of the independent variable t).
ready1_open_rewrite.title: MM-Math open-ended problem
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: In the Cartesian coordinate system, point O is the origin. The parabola $y = ax^2 + bx + 3$ passes through points $B(-3, 0)$ and $C(1, 0)$, and intersects the y-axis at point A. As shown in Figure 1, point P lies on the parabola. A line through point P parallel to the y-axis intersects the line segment $AB$ at point D. Denoting the x-coordinate of point P as $t$, and the length of segment $PD$ as $d$, find the functional expression of $d$ in terms of $t$ (it is not required to state the domain of the independent variable $t$).
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: \textbf{Solution:} \[ \begin{aligned} &\because a=-1, b=-2 \\ &\therefore y=x^2-2x+3 \\ &\text{when } x=0, y=3 \\ &\therefore A(0, 3) \\ &\text{Let the line } AB: y=kx+b' \\ &\because B(-3, 0) \\ &\therefore \left\{ \begin{array}{l} b'=3 \\ -3k+b'=0 \end{array} \right. \\ &\therefore \left\{ \begin{array}{l} k=1 \\ b'=3 \end{array} \right. \\ &\therefore \text{The equation of line } AB \text{ is } y=x+3 \\ &\because DP \parallel \text{ the y-axis}, \\ &\therefore P, O \text{ have the same x-coordinate } t \\ &\therefore p(t, -t^2-2t+3), O(t, t+3) \\ &\therefore d=-t^2-2t+3-(t+3) \\ &=-t^2-3t \\ &\therefore d=\boxed{-t^2-3t} \end{aligned} \]

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the given picture, the left side is Figure 1. Figure 1 shows a parabola opening downward, intersecting the x-axis on the left side at B and on the right side at C, and intersecting the y-axis at A; point P is above the left branch of the parabola. From P, draw a vertical line segment downward, intersecting segment AB at D, so PD is parallel to the y-axis, and in the position shown in the figure, P is above D. There is also Figure 2 on the right side, but this problem only uses Figure 1. Then reason: according to the meaning of the problem, the parabola y=ax^2+bx+3 passes through B(-3,0) and C(1,0), so its two zeros are -3 and 1, and it can be set as y=k(x+3)(x-1). The constant term after expansion is -3k, while the constant term of the original expression is 3, so -3k=3, giving k=-1. Therefore the equation of the parabola is y=-(x+3)(x-1)=-x^2-2x+3. When x=0, y=3, so A=(0,3). The line AB passes through A(0,3) and B(-3,0), and its slope is (3-0)/(0-(-3))=1, therefore the equation of line AB is y=x+3. Let the x-coordinate of point P be t. Then P is on the parabola, so y_P=-t^2-2t+3. Because PD is vertical, D and P have the same x-coordinate t; also D is on the line y=x+3 where segment AB lies, so y_D=t+3. From Figure 1 it can be seen that in the relevant position P is above D, so d=PD=y_P-y_D=(-t^2-2t+3)-(t+3)=-t^2-3t.
